title: Equational consequence and term-model completeness
summary: Derive identities by equality, congruence and substitution rules, and construct a term quotient that refutes every nonderivable equation.
abstract: An operation that always returns its first argument also returns the first argument of a nested application. Such deductions replace variables by compound expressions and chain equations together. We give a finite proof calculus for identities in arbitrary functional signatures and show that its rules derive exactly the equations true in every nonempty algebra satisfying the stated laws. The key construction takes terms as elements and identifies precisely those pairs whose equality is derivable. This quotient satisfies all the original laws under every assignment, while its canonical assignment separates any pair that cannot be proved equal. Every consequence therefore already follows from finitely many of the original identities. Concrete projection algebras show how to refute proposed deductions and why substitution requires truth under every assignment.

based_on.title: A Course in Universal Algebra (2012 update)
based_on.pages: Chapter II, §14, pp. 93–96: Theorems 14.12, 14.17 and 14.19; Definitions 14.13–14.18
